continuity.arc_goal: Implement promise objects and unified linking model supporting entity linking (objects) and invocation linking (workflows) with objects as persistent anchors

progress_update.summary: Fixed proto field number bugs and LinkCommand message type ID mismatch that caused SDK panics. Then evolved the linked workflows design through an extensive design session — arrived at a unified linking model where objects and workflow invocations are the two node types in a graph, with objects as the only anchors. Worked through storage schema: evolve existing ServiceStatus and InvocationStatus tables for node lifecycle, add new ServiceEdges and InvocationEdges tables for the graph edges.
progress_update.goal: Evolve the linked workflows/promise objects design into a unified linking model supporting entity linking (objects) and invocation linking (workflows), with objects as persistent anchors, fact accumulation, and GC by reachability from live objects.
accomplished: Fixed ResolveCompletionNotificationMessage proto field numbers (void=13→4, failure=15→6) and result_completion_id (field 1→11) to match protocol conventions
Fixed LinkCommand message type ID from 0x040F to 0x0415 — root cause of SDK panic when sending LinkCommand
Added test asserting all command/notification type ID pairs share the same offset
Designed unified linking model: two node types (ObjectId=ServiceId, WorkflowInvocationId=ServiceId+InvocationUuid), four link combinations, one anchoring rule (live objects anchor everything)
Designed storage schema: evolve ServiceStatus (add Resolved), keep InvocationStatus, new ServiceEdges and InvocationEdges tables with LinkedTo/LinkedFrom edge labels
progress_update.now: Design session complete. Ready to write the design doc capturing the unified linking model and storage schema decisions.
next_steps: Write design doc capturing the unified linking model (supersedes promise_objects.md and linked_workflows_mvp.md)
Implement LinkChild outbox message to differentiate workflow links (start handler) from object links (establish link only)
Add ServiceEdges and InvocationEdges KeyKind entries and table implementations
constraints: Proto field numbers must match between server and sdk-shared-core
All tables are logical (2-byte KeyKind prefix) within one RocksDB CF per partition — no write amplification from multiple tables
InvocationId is (partition_key, invocation_uuid) — no ServiceId, so CompletedInvocation.invocation_target carries the service association
WriteBatch provides atomic writes across multiple logical tables in the same CF
Objects link as entities (ServiceId), workflow invocations link as invocations (InvocationId) — never reversed
ResolveCompletionNotification reserved fields: server includes 7,8 which SDK omits — server version is more conservative/correct
decisions: Two node types: ObjectId(ServiceId) and WorkflowInvocationId(ServiceId, InvocationUuid) — objects link as entities, workflows link as invocations
One anchoring rule: live objects are the only anchors, everything else is transient unless reachable from a live object
Edge labels: LinkedTo/LinkedFrom replacing ParentOf/ChildOf — directional without prescribing hierarchy
Storage: evolve existing ServiceStatus (add Resolved) and InvocationStatus (unchanged), new ServiceEdges ('se') and InvocationEdges ('ie') tables
VirtualObjectStatus becomes: Unlocked | Locked(InvocationId) | Resolved(ResponseResult) — three clean states
Mutation models: objects = transactional KV state (frozen on resolve), workflows = append-only journal (sealed on completion)
Separate edge tables by local node type — no local_type discriminator needed, table IS the discriminator
ResolveCommandMessage uses same wire layout as OutputCommandMessage plus result_completion_id=11 (completable+fallible)
open_questions: Should workflow invocations get invocation-scoped KV state in addition to journal? (discussed but not decided)
Where does revision counter live — on ObjectStatus record or keep as \x00__revision in state table?
Remote side key encoding in edge tables — how to encode the variable-width remote node ID with type discriminator
Should SDK align to server's reserved declaration (add fields 7, 8) or should we drop them to match SDK?
risks: The design is a significant evolution from the current link table — migration path from existing LinkRelation/ChildOf/ParentOf needs planning
